ctor.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): `Card.energy_cost` (`sts2_rl/cards/base.py`) now short-circuits on `self._energy_cost < 0` as its first check, returning the raw canonical value before consulting `_free_this_turn` / `_cost_this_turn` / `_cost_this_combat` / `_cost_delta_this_turn` -- mirrors `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers`'s `if (_base < 0) return num;` short-circuit (`CardEnergyCost.cs:101-104`; the record's `:100-103` cite is one line of decompiler drift), which runs before any local or global modifier. All 29 unplayable curse/status/quest cards now set `self._energy_cost = -1` in `_init_vars` (previously 0), each verified individually against its own C# `base(-1, CardType.X, ...)` constructor -- no exceptions, no ascension-gated cost variant. Readers audit (every non-cards/ `energy_cost` hit read in context): combat play/auto-play/valid_actions/action-mask sites gate on `is_playable` first and never see -1; every global-modifier site routes through `hooks.modify_card_energy_cost`, whose dispatcher ends `return max(0, cost)` -- the sim's analogue of C#'s `Math.Max(0, GetWithModifiers(...))` in `GetAmountToSpend`/`GetResolved` (`CardEnergyCost.cs:134-141`) -- so what is SPENT and what the observation encoder reads (`full_env.py` card_features via `previews.py` preview_card_energy_cost) are byte-for-byte unchanged. The three previously-known readers (`relics/mummified_hand.py`, `potions.py` TouchOfInsanity, `cards/event_cards.py` Enlightenment) remain correct, confirmed by unit tests. NOT closed here: `selectors.py`'s `scripted_card_selector` 'to_draw_top' purpose (Headbutt/Thinking Ahead) ranks by raw `card.energy_cost` unclamped -- a sim-only heuristic with no C# analogue; a curse in a Headbutt-eligible discard pile now ranks below-cost instead of tying at 0. No test exercises it; filed in GAP-QUEUE.md's 'Named work with no entry of its own'. New pins: test/test_unplayable_cost.py (15 tests).  The text it replaced read: Type/rarity/target map exactly (CURSE / CURSE / NONE), but the canonical energy cost is **-1** in C# (`base(-1, ...)`, BadLuck.cs:27-30) and **0** in the sim (`self._energy_cost = 0`, bad_luck.py:34). Same divergence as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry and, per rule 3, the same verdict: `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), making the game's unplayable curse immune to every cost modifier, while the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain in `Card.energy_cost` (cards/base.py:222-232). DORMANT for the same executed reason -- the three ported cost readers (`relics/mummified_hand.py:25` and `potions.py:168` filter `> 0`; `cards/event_cards.py:328` skips `<= 1`) and the one pool filter (`events/infested_automaton.py:35`, over `pool_card_ids()`, which holds no curses) all treat -1 and 0 alike. Live as soon as any effect reads an unplayable card's cost without a `> 0` filter.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: nothing -- the sim inlines 13 at the damage site (bad_luck.py:43)
CanonicalVars.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 24.) All 23 cards now store their printed C# var under a `_`-attribute (or, for 3 cards whose C# var is a live/computed value at display time -- guilty, normality, expect_a_fight -- a `magic_number` property override; wither similarly overrides `base_damage`) so `Card.base_damage`/`base_block`/`base_hp_loss`/`magic_number` report the C# value instead of the 0/None default. Two additive base.py changes: `_frail` added to `_MAGIC_ATTRS` (shame) and a new `base_gold` property (debt, spoils_map -- GoldVar had no base property at all). feel_no_pain's `_block` was renamed to `_power_amount` (fixing a WRONG value, not just a missing one -- `base_block` no longer misreports it as block-granting; matches Rage/Corruption/Stampede's DynamicVar('Power', ...) convention). Combat behavior / dealt numbers are byte-identical in every case -- a printed-number / observation-encoder fix only. 3 of the 23 (debt, spoils_map, rolling_boulder's secondary IncrementAmount) have NO obs-vector change despite the API fix (full_env.py has no base_gold read site; magic_number carries one number per card and _power_amount dominates rolling_boulder's scan) -- documented, not closed further. CHECKPOINT NOTE for training: encoded VALUES changed for the other 20 cards in feature slots f[17]/f[18] damage, f[20]/f[21] block, f[22] hp_loss, f[23] magic_number; obs LAYOUT unchanged. Pins: test/test_printed_vars.py (48 tests).  The text it replaced read: `new HpLossVar(13m)` (BadLuck.cs:25) is a printed card var; the sim declares no `_hp_loss` in `_init_vars`, so `Card.base_hp_loss` (cards/base.py:202-210) returns its 0 default for this card and the number 13 exists only as a literal inside `on_turn_end_in_hand`. The DEALT damage is identical (13 either way), so no player-visible combat outcome differs -- but the sim's own printed-number API misreports the card, and it is read: `full_env.py:488` encodes `card.base_hp_loss / ABS_SCALE` into the observation vector, so a policy sees Bad Luck as a harmless 0-HP-loss curse. Recorded as a gap rather than a deliberate divergence because nothing in the code marks it intentional and every other numbered card in this batch does declare its var. DORMANT with respect to game fidelity (no game-observable difference); LIVE with respect to the sim's observation encoder. The concrete fix is a one-line `self._hp_loss = 13` in `_init_vars` -- NOT applied, per the no-engine-edits rule.

OnTurnEndInHand.rationale: `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.HpLoss.BaseValue, ValueProp.Unblockable | ValueProp.Unpowered | ValueProp.Move, this)` (BadLuck.cs:35) == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, 13, card=self, props=DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS)`. `DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS` is exactly `UNBLOCKABLE | UNPOWERED | MOVE` (valueprops.py:38). Self-targeted, and both sides pass no dealer (C# omits the dealer argument entirely, the sim leaves `dealer` at its None default), so no AfterDamageGiven attribution fires on either side. Presentation, folded in: BadLuck.cs:34 awaits Cmd.Wait(0.25f) before the damage -- pacing only.

OnPlay.rationale: BadLuck.cs declares no OnPlay; the card is Unplayable. The sim's abstract method is satisfied with a `pass`.

guards.what: the damage is UNBLOCKABLE, so block never absorbs it, and UNPOWERED, so Strength/Vulnerable/Weak never scale it
guards.rationale: `is_powered_attack` is `MOVE in props and UNPOWERED not in props` (valueprops.py:49), which is False here on both sides; and the UNBLOCKABLE branch of the sim's damage pipeline skips block exactly as C#'s does. The MOVE bit is still set on both sides, so effects keyed on 'card or monster move' (Vambrace's `IsCardOrMonsterMove()`) see it identically.
